To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PSOs deploy 16 organizational actions to implement OI and these actions collectively constitute their dynamic capabilities of sensing and seizing.

(1) PSOs' dynamic capability of sensing is enacted and collectively used by PSOs through 16 organizational actions to engage in OIs; (2) in all of these organizational activities, IT plays a key role; and (3) PSOs' IT-enabled OI initiatives are more effective when they are supported by a strong organizational culture and a strong organizational structure.
PSOs can use IT to implement 16 organizational actions that can be used to deploy OI initiatives and to develop their dynamic capabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organizational actions that PSOs can deploy to engage in OIs and the role of IT in this process.
how PSOs enact their dynamic capabilities through OI and the role IT plays in these processes.
how PSOs can use their dynamic capabilities to enact OI through the use of IT and to create value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PSOs' use of OI is enabled and facilitated by their dynamic capabilities, and that the role of IT in OI is central and pervasive.
PSOs can use OI to enhance their dynamic capabilities and IT can be a key enabler of this process.
OI in the public sector is a dynamic capability enacted by PSOs' organizational actions that are facilitated by the use of IT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OI initiatives in PSOs are enabled and facilitated by the deployment of a set of organizational actions that are collectively used to enact the dynamic capabilities of sensing and seizing.
IT is a key enabler of OI in PSOs.
PSOs' ability to implement OI is contingent on their dynamic capabilities, which in turn, are supported by the use of IT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PSOs' OI initiatives can be supported through a combination of organizational actions and IT.
IT is a critical enabler of OI initiatives.
PSOs need to develop their dynamic capabilities and deploy IT in order to implement OI.
